methodology_note: Repo-surface track: this product is distributed as a repository (library/CLI) with no web product surface, so the score derives ONLY from measurable public-repository signals — documentation, licensing, maintenance activity, releases, traction, agent-consumability. Each checklist item carries its evidence. Score ceiling 82/100: VITAL requires hands-on behavioral testing that repo signals cannot provide. Replaces a 2026-06/07 stub that carried a default score with no evidence.

hlido_opinion.headline: A well-adopted, provider-neutral agent-skill and harness-design guide — reference material, not a runnable product.
hlido_opinion.body: agents-best-practices is a provider-neutral agent skill and best-practices guide for building agentic harnesses across Codex, Claude Code and similar tools. It is reference/skill content rather than an executable service, and on that footing it does well: 2.1K stars is strong adoption for a guide, it is MIT-licensed, the README documents how to consume it, and it is actively maintained. It was previously miscategorized as Image & Design; it is squarely Frameworks & Eval. The right expectation to set is that its value is the quality of the guidance it encodes — which repo signals cannot grade — while the 82 reflects that it is a healthy, permissively-licensed, well-adopted, agent-consumable repository.

tier_rationale: STEADY (82), the repo-surface ceiling: reachable, MIT-licensed, documented install/usage, 2.1K stars, recent commits, and a CLI/agent-skill consumption path. Not VITAL because the substance — whether the best practices actually improve agent outcomes — needs hands-on evaluation the repo signals cannot provide, and there are no releases or CI to point to.
what_it_does_well: Strong adoption for a guide/skill repo (2.1K stars)
Provider-neutral — targets Codex, Claude Code and general agentic harnesses
MIT-licensed with a documented consumption path
what_it_fails_at: Not a runnable product — it is reference/skill content
No releases and no CI workflows
The quality/impact of the guidance itself was not evaluated
best_for: Engineers designing agent harnesses who want a provider-neutral starting point
Teams standardizing agent-skill conventions across Codex/Claude Code
not_recommended_for: Buyers looking for an executable agent or service
Anyone needing benchmarked evidence that the practices improve outcomes
